facts.name: Bearded Iris
facts.notes: Ruffled flowers in late spring over sword-like leaves. Plant the rhizomes at the soil surface; divide every 3-4 years.

fall.why: old leaves are where iris borers lay their eggs

sources.title: Purdue Extension: Cut Back Perennials Now or Later?
sources.note: Cut iris in fall to reduce iris borer sites; cut peonies, bee balm and phlox; otherwise wait until several hard frosts have killed the tops.

sources.title: University of Minnesota Extension: Upper Midwest Home Garden Care Calendar
sources.note: Divide bearded iris late July to early August and peonies from late August; plant spring bulbs from September to mid-November.
